original_question: Let Lambda_n be the set of partitions of n ordered by refinement. Determine the Mobius function mu(lambda, rho) of this refinement poset.
target_in_paper: Problem 19 in Section 2 ("Problems of 2025"), attributed to [Stan2012, Ch. 3 Exer. 135(b)]: "Let Λ_n be the set of all p(n) partitions of the integer n ≥ 0. Order Λ_n by refinement. Determine the Möbius function μ(λ, ρ) of Λ_n." The paper adds the contextual remark that this is trivial when λ = (1^n) and easy when λ = (1^{n-2},2).
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper's target almost exactly: it uses the same poset Λ_n of partitions of a fixed integer n, the same refinement order, and the same task of determining the Möbius function. It is also correctly focused on integer partitions rather than a broader family of posets.
missing_details: The paper explicitly quantifies over integers n ≥ 0.
It should be made explicit that Λ_n consists of integer partitions of n, with |Λ_n| = p(n).

To be fully stand-alone, the refinement order should be defined explicitly: λ ≤ ρ means that ρ is obtained from λ by repeatedly merging parts, equivalently the parts of λ can be grouped so that their sums are the parts of ρ.
The Möbius function should be identified as the poset Möbius function μ_{Λ_n}(λ,ρ), defined for comparable pairs λ ≤ ρ in Λ_n.
The paper records two contextual boundary cases: λ = (1^n) is trivial and λ = (1^{n-2},2) is easy.
There are no ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses here; this is a purely finite-poset question.
refined_question: For each integer n ≥ 0, let Λ_n be the finite poset of all integer partitions of n, ordered by refinement; that is, λ ≤ ρ if ρ can be obtained from λ by repeatedly merging parts, equivalently if the parts of λ can be grouped so that their group-sums are exactly the parts of ρ. Determine the poset Möbius function μ_{Λ_n}(λ,ρ) for every comparable pair λ ≤ ρ in Λ_n.
justification: The paper is a notebook of open problems, and your draft clearly targets Problem 19 in Section 2 rather than any other item. The draft already matches the mathematical core of the paper's wording very closely, so the refinement only makes the hidden assumptions explicit: n ≥ 0, integer partitions, the precise meaning of refinement, and that μ is the Möbius function on comparable pairs in the finite poset Λ_n. I did not broaden the question beyond the exact problem listed in the paper, and I did not add unrelated algebraic structure because none appears in the paper's statement.
